issues.label: Reasonable suspicion for initial jaywalking stop
issues.why: Court must determine whether police had reasonable suspicion to justify the investigative stop of K.J.

issues.label: Whether an investigatory stop actually occurred
issues.why: K.J. fled before officers effected a seizure, raising whether Fourth Amendment protections attached.

issues.label: Flight as basis for obstruction probable cause
issues.why: Court must assess whether running from police alone supports probable cause for obstructing official business.

issues.label: Legality of arrest and probable cause
issues.why: K.J. challenges whether police had probable cause to arrest him.

issues.label: Whether flight from unlawful stop is privileged
issues.why: If the initial stop was unlawful, K.J.'s flight may not constitute obstruction.

issues.label: Attenuation and fruit of poisonous tree
issues.why: Court must decide whether evidence found after flight is tainted by any illegal stop.

issues.label: High-crime area relevance to suspicion
issues.why: Whether the neighborhood's reputation properly factored into reasonable suspicion analysis.

issues.label: Collective knowledge/fellow officer doctrine
issues.why: Stop relied on radioed observations from other officers, implicating imputed knowledge.

issues.label: Standing to challenge apartment search
issues.why: Whether K.J. had a reasonable expectation of privacy in the apartment he entered.

issues.label: Legality of warrantless apartment search
issues.why: The gun was found in an apartment searched without an apparent warrant or consent.

issues.label: Sufficiency: carrying concealed weapon
issues.why: Officers never saw the gun on K.J.'s person or in the bag, questioning concealment proof.

issues.label: Sufficiency: tampering with evidence
issues.why: State must prove K.J. concealed or moved the gun knowing of an official proceeding.

issues.label: Knowledge of investigation element for tampering
issues.why: Tampering requires awareness that an investigation was likely underway.

issues.label: Sufficiency: obstructing official business
issues.why: Court must find an affirmative act hampering police, and mere flight may be insufficient.

issues.label: Whether jaywalking is 'lawful duty' for obstruction
issues.why: Obstruction requires interference with police performing an authorized function.

issues.label: Manifest weight: jaywalking adjudication
issues.why: K.J. challenges whether evidence supports the traffic offense finding.

issues.label: Address discrepancies in citations/reports
issues.why: Inconsistent offense locations may undermine reliability of jaywalking proof.

issues.label: Dismissal and refiling of jaywalking citation
issues.why: Court should consider validity of the December refiling after dismissal.

issues.label: Operability of firearm as element
issues.why: CCW/tampering may require the weapon qualify as operable deadly weapon.

issues.label: Constructive vs. actual possession of gun
issues.why: Whether K.J. possessed the gun found in the utility closet must be established.

issues.label: Weight of K.J.'s statement admitting gun
issues.why: K.J.'s admission that someone gave him the gun bears on possession/concealment.

issues.label: Standard of review for suppression ruling
issues.why: Court applies mixed factual-deference and de novo legal review to suppression.

issues.label: Standard of review for sufficiency and manifest weight
issues.why: Distinct legal standards govern each evidentiary challenge raised.

issues.label: Proper application of Terry vs. probable cause
issues.why: Trial court's delineation between Terry stop and probable cause must be evaluated.
